findings.title: Core alignment: boundaries, determinism, and the 50ms target are preserved
findings.description: The design matches slice plan entry 7 of `100-slices.behavior-engine.md:37` (same five forces, same protocol+caller update-in-one-slice requirement). It honors 100-arch's "Pluggable spatial queries" and "Clean boundaries": `SpatialQuery.query_radius` is unchanged, padding lives in a new `engine/neighbors.py` (`:168`), and the spatial layer is explicitly "unaware of padding". Centralizing self-exclusion in the builder (`:88`) removes duplicated per-force filtering, which follows CLAUDE.md's DRY principle. Determinism is protected by float64 equivalence tests (`:190`, `:219`). The tick-budget NFR from `300-arch.worldserver-foundation.md:69`/`:81` (20–60Hz) is restated with a specific target — 100 agents, `query_radius: 50.0`, 50ms budget, pre-slice 58–60ms — at `:23` and `:211-215`. No new I/O or message paths are introduced, so no network failure-mode spec is required.

findings.title: Zero-neighbor rows produce non-zero forces under the documented pattern
findings.description: The representative cohesion pattern computes `center_of_mass = sum / max(counts, 1)` then `cohesion = (center_of_mass - self_positions) * weights`. For a `counts[i] == 0` row, the gathered values are zeroed, so `center_of_mass` is `[0,0]`, and the force becomes `-self_positions[i] * weight` — non-zero for any agent away from the origin. The same holds for AlignmentForce and LeadershipForce (`(0 - agent_velocity) * weight`). This directly contradicts "Handling Zero-Neighbor Agents" (`:170-172`: "The masked reduction produces zero force for that agent, matching current behavior") and the loop implementations' `if len(neighbors) == 0: continue`, and therefore leaves the primary functional requirement at `:190` (numerically identical output within float64 tolerance) unmet. Since this pattern is declared the template for all five rewrites (`:105`, `:245`), the defect propagates. State the explicit mechanism: multiply the final force by a `counts > 0` mask (or zero those output rows) for every reduction-based force, and add it to the equivalence tests' zero-neighbor cases (`:193`, `:259`).

findings.title: Full-population N×2 output scatter is never specified
findings.description: `NeighborData` is shaped `(n_active, max_neighbors)` (`:73-79`) and the force pattern produces an `(n_active, 2)` result (`:105`, `:118`), but the design never says how that result is placed into the `BulkForce` return value. Slice 100's protocol contract (`100-slice.agent-state-and-tick-function.md:141-152`) requires a **full-population N×2 array with zeros for non-active agents**; 100-arch's "Subset-evaluable tick" principle requires the same. Without an explicit `result = zeros((N,2)); result[eval_indices] = computed` step — and an explicit statement that `NeighborData` rows are aligned to `eval_indices` order — the `active_indices` subset success criterion at `:193` has no defined mechanism. Add both to the shared pattern and a test asserting zero forces for inactive agents.

findings.title: `-1` padding is actually dereferenced; masked-gather failure modes are unhandled
findings.description: The doc states padded entries are `-1` and "never dereferenced thanks to `mask`", but the very next section gathers with `state.positions[neighbor_data.indices]` (`:111`) and only zeroes the result afterwards (`neighbor_pos[~mask] = 0.0`, `:114`). In NumPy `-1` is a valid index (last agent), so it *is* dereferenced; correctness silently depends on every force applying the mask after the gather, before any reduction. That is a hidden invariant and a silent fallback value, contrary to CLAUDE.md's "Never use silent fallback values". It also leaves computational failure modes unspecified: SeparationForce's inverse-square division (`:123`) can produce divide-by-zero / NaN / warnings on zero-distance and padded rows before the mask is applied. Define one safe policy — e.g. pad with `0` (or `np.take` with a valid index) and apply `np.where(mask, ...)` before any arithmetic — and state explicitly how invalid rows and zero distances are neutralized in the distance/radius computation so NaN cannot reach `np.sum`.

findings.title: Scale NFR is not restated, and the design still carries O(n) Python overhead in the hot path
findings.description: The parent architecture states a specific NFR: "Support tens of thousands of agents at full behavioral fidelity on a single CPU process" and "The hot loop must be structured for vectorized computation over arrays of agent state, not object-by-object iteration" (`100-arch.behavior-engine.md:36`); `:88` additionally warns that per-tick allocation creates GC pressure and requires `out=`/preallocated buffers; `300-arch.worldserver-foundation.md:91` asserts memory is never the bottleneck. This doc restates none of that target and validates only n=100 (~80KB, `:146`), deflecting higher counts with "For n=100 this is negligible. At higher n, profile weights can be precomputed per tick **if needed**" (`:136`) and "a CSR representation may become necessary ... future work" (`:148`). Meanwhile the layout is O(n × max_neighbors) per tick plus five fresh `(n, max_neighbors, 2)` gathers (`:105`) — quadratic in the clustered case the slice exists to fix, with no buffer reuse. The claim of "constant Python overhead, regardless of agent count" (`:19`) is also inaccurate: step 2 remains a per-agent query loop and the new step 3 builder is described only as "a single pass to pad, mask, and self-exclude" (`:101`) over jagged lists, i.e. a new per-agent Python loop in the hot path, which slice 100's success criteria prohibit. Restate the concrete scale target (e.g. 10K agents at 20Hz/50ms), bound or chunk `max_neighbors`, specify preallocated buffers for the gathers, and either vectorize the jagged→padded construction or state its measured cost against the 50ms budget.

findings.title: Breaking protocol change is not reconciled with the declared consumer slices
findings.description: Frontmatter declares `interfaces: [103-predator-prey-dynamics, 105-spatial-query-optimization]`, but neither counterpart matches this contract. `103-slice.predator-prey-dynamics.md:398-399` states "The tick function remains unchanged. Forces receive the same `(state, neighbor_lists, profiles, active_indices)` arguments", with `FlightForce`/`PursuitForce` iterating `neighbor_lists[list_idx]` in a Python loop (`:444-452`, `:507-515`); `304-slice.environment-layer-integration.md:210` documents the same old signature for future environment-aware forces. 109 says predator-prey forces will "consume this instead of raw lists" (`:178`) yet never says 103's design must be revised, nor that 109 becomes a prerequisite — so "all `BulkForce` implementations must be updated in this slice" (`:164`) is undefined if 103 lands first. Conversely, 109 assigns the "Batch spatial query interface" to slice 105 (`:44`, `:184`: "When slice 105 introduces a batch query"), while plan entry 6 (`100-slices.behavior-engine.md:34`) specifies a spatial hash "behind the existing query interface" with no batch-query variant. Also, `WorldBoundsRepulsor`/`ConstantDrift`/`VelocityDrag` appear in "Excluded" (`:43`) yet step 8 requires changing their signatures (`:251`) and `:191` says they "continue to function unchanged" — clarify "unchanged behavior, changed signature". Name the coordination explicitly: either declare 109 a prerequisite for 103 and note the required design update, or list those force implementations in scope; and remove the batch-query handoff to 105.

findings.title: GPU-readiness is scope creep and its claim contradicts the architecture's GPU constraints
findings.description: GPU offload is explicitly future work in the architecture ("at the 1M+ entity tier", `100-arch.behavior-engine.md:102`; `300-slices.worldserver-foundation.md` Future Work item 2), yet it is used here as the deciding justification for the padded representation (`:27`, `:146-148`, `:180`). The claim is also unsupported: `100-arch...:102` requires a GPU-compatible force path with "no Python-level per-agent branching, no dynamic allocation, and no callbacks into Python during the hot loop", while this design retains a per-force Python list comprehension over n agents (`:132-136`), fresh `(n,k,2)` allocations per force call (`:111`), and a Python builder pass (`:101`). Cut or defer: the "Enables future GPU offload" value bullet, the "GPU-ready data layout — padded arrays can be transferred to GPU compute buffers directly" provides bullet (`:180`), and the CSR/COO deliberation about 100K+ entity tiers (`:142-148`) — choose the padded array on present-requirement merits only. For proportionality, `Implementation Notes > Development Approach` (`:242-254`) largely restates "Included" and `Testing Strategy` (`:258-262`) restates "Success Criteria"/"Verification Walkthrough"; these can be trimmed rather than adding a second specification of the same work for a 3/5-effort slice.

structured_findings.summary: Core alignment: boundaries, determinism, and the 50ms target are preserved
Zero-neighbor rows produce non-zero forces under the documented pattern
Full-population N×2 output scatter is never specified
`-1` padding is actually dereferenced; masked-gather failure modes are unhandled
Scale NFR is not restated, and the design still carries O(n) Python overhead in the hot path
Breaking protocol change is not reconciled with the declared consumer slices
GPU-readiness is scope creep and its claim contradicts the architecture's GPU constraints
